extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment & Discipline, and counsel handling USPTO disciplinary matters
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, procedural rules, and sanctions governing USPTO-registered patent practitioners arising from disciplinary proceedings and settlement agreements. Covers jurisdiction, specific disciplinary rule violations, mitigation factors, sanctions, reinstatement, publication, and related procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction and authority to approve settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over the matter and authority to approve a Proposed Settlement Agreement pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order affirms that the Director may approve settlement agreements resolving disciplinary actions under the cited statutory and regulatory provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed Settlement Agreement requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Proposed Settlement Agreement must satisfy the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.26 to resolve disciplinary actions by agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Proposed Settlement Agreement submitted by the parties must set forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and agreed sanctions and comply with the procedural and substantive requirements of § 11.26.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowingly giving false or misleading information to the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation by knowingly giving false or misleading information to the Office, charged under 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(b)(3), (b)(4), (b)(5) and (b)(6), via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(2)(ii), and 37 C.F.R. § 10.85(a)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order finds that providing a false receipted postcard and relying on it in petitions to revive an abandoned application constitutes knowingly providing false or misleading information to the USPTO; such conduct supports disciplinary sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglecting a matter entrusted to the practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c) for neglecting a matter entrusted to the respondent (here, allowing an application to become abandoned and related misstatements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neglect of client matters (failure to act timely or properly prosecute applications) is a separate disciplinary basis and is considered in determining sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factors considered in discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors mitigating discipline include no prior disciplinary history, misconduct appearing aberrational, employer-imposed sanctions (e.g., probation), cooperation with the OED investigation, and remorse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director considered the respondent's over eighteen years with no prior discipline, the aberrational nature of the misconduct, employer sanctions, and full cooperation when agreeing to the settlement and selecting sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension from practice before the USPTO (sanction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent suspended from practicing patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO for twenty-four (24) months commencing on the date the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The suspension is the primary sanction imposed by the settlement. The order describes the duration and that reinstatement procedures are available under regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to practice to facilitate compliance with § 11.58(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice beginning on the date the Final Order is signed and expiring thirty (30) days after that date solely to facilitate compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited recognition is narrowly time-limited (30 days) and exists only to allow the respondent to take steps required by § 11.58(b) (e.g., winding down matters, giving notice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must comply with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 during suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with § 11.58 (duties of suspended practitioners, such as notice to clients and arrangements for transfer of files) is mandatory and is a stated condition of the Final Order and for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation of name from Customer Numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate Respondent's name from the Customer Numbers with which she is associated and dissociate her PKI certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of the sanction, the Office will remove practitioner association from electronic access identifiers to prevent practice before the Office while suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on applying for or obtaining a Customer Number while suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may not apply for, or obtain a USPTO Customer Number or have her name added to a Customer Number, unless and until she is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibits any attempt to regain electronic access to the USPTO systems during suspension; reinstatement is required to regain such privileges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for reinstatement timing and procedure (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may file a petition for reinstatement at any time after two (2) months from the date the Final Order is signed, requesting reinstatement effective prior to expiration of the 24-month suspension, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the suspension term is 24 months, the respondent is eligible to petition for early reinstatement after two months; such petitions must follow § 11.60 rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement substantive standards (37 C.F.R. § 11.60(c) and § 11.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain reinstatement the petitioner must show proof satisfactory to the OED Director that: (1) the petitioner has the good moral character and reputation, competency, and learning in law required under 37 C.F.R. § 11.7 for admission; (2) resumption of practice will not be detrimental to administration of justice or subversive to the public interest; (3) petitioner has complied with provisions of the Final Order while suspended; and (4) petitioner has complied with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement is discretionary and requires demonstrable rehabilitation, competence, and compliance with the Final Order and suspension-related duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation upon reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: If reinstated, Respondent shall serve an eighteen (18) month period of probation beginning on the date the OED Director reinstates Respondent pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probationary conditions apply post-reinstatement and noncompliance during probation may trigger further proceedings and sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause process and possible additional suspension for probation violations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes the respondent failed to comply with the Final Order or any Disciplinary Rule during probation, the OED Director shall (A) issue an Order to Show Cause why the USPTO Director should not immediately suspend the respondent for up to an additional twenty-two (22) months; (B) send the Order to the respondent's last address of record; and (C) grant the respondent fifteen (15) days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After consideration of any response, if the OED Director remains of that opinion, the Director will deliver the Order to Show Cause, response, and evidence to the USPTO Director and request entry of an immediate additional suspension up to 22 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and procedures if suspended during probation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent is suspended during probation the OED Director shall disseminate information in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59; the USPTO shall dissociate the respondent's name from Customer Numbers and PKI certificates; and the respondent may not apply for a Customer Number until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These steps mirror initial-suspension consequences and include public notice and loss of electronic access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of discipline (OED Reading Room, Official Gazette, § 11.59 notices)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room and shall publish a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette. Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, notice of public discipline and reasons shall be given to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where respondent is admitted, to courts where respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order includes the exact Notice of Suspension text and states that disciplinary decisions are posted publicly; dissemination to other agencies and courts is mandatory per § 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the settlement prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, when addressing further complaints or as an aggravating factor in future disciplinary proceedings or to rebut statements by or on respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prior settlement and Final Order may be used to increase penalties or counter claims of rehabilitation in later matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The settlement allocates no award of costs between the parties; each party is responsible for its own expenses.
